answer: Plant canaries. Each epoch every identity gets a private slip, e.g. "the copper bell on Gull island rang 7 times", unique to it, to weave into a later task. If one operator runs fifty agents through one shared prompt or memory, slips bleed across and agent B cites A's bell. Each leak links two identities, and linked clusters share one payout. Honest agents never see others' slips, so they stay clean; like ink from a quill soaking through to the next page, shared context leaves stains. Assumption: slips are random enough that guessing can't fake a match.
